source.prompt: (the red-tail's) A red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis), one adult bird soaring in mid-air, wings fully spread out flat to the sides and symmetrical, about 125 cm wingspan and 55 cm long, shaped to read from below and from above. Broad rounded wings with a straight leading edge and five separated, fingered primary feathers at each wingtip. Short, broad brick-red tail fanned wide into a rounded fan. Legs and feet tucked up under the body. Big rounded head and short hooked bill projecting ahead of the wings. Pale underwing with a dark leading-edge bar and a dark wrist mark, pale breast with a dark belly band. Not an eagle, not a falcon. Single bird, no base, no perch. Game-ready, clean closed mesh.

rig: bird rig template, flight mesh, exactly as client/assets/redtail.glb (the client draws the raptors with the hawk's soaring and the gulls with the vulture's circling glides): PART BODY 0, TAIL 3 (pivot at the tail root), HEAD 6 (head, neck and bill, pivot at the neck's base), WING_L/R 4/5 (the arm, pivot at the shoulder, weight ramped in over the wing root), HAND_L/R 9/10 (pivot at the wrist, weight ramped over the hand); collapse 0 (the wings never fold). extras.rig keys as the hawk's: kind 'bird', wing (shoulder [0.055, 0.11, 0.02]), wrist [0.273, 0.133, 0.02], tail [0.0, 0.086, -0.074], head [0.0, 0.102, 0.151], span_m 1.3, dihedral_deg -1.6 (shoulder to wingtip). Origin 0.11 m below the shoulder line. No skin.
accuracy_notes: Field marks: white head, body and tail; medium grey mantle and upperwing with a white trailing edge; black outer primaries (the outer fifth of the span, above and below) with a white mirror; the underwing white with grey flight feathers; a yellow bill with a black ring and a red gonys spot (lod0); a dark eye. No legs show (tucked), so the greenish-yellow legs are not drawn. Reads as a medium gull with black wingtips and a medium-grey mantle, darker than the glaucous-winged and paler than the western. Still open: the wingtip is one black block with one white mirror (a real one has two mirrors and white apical spots); the bill's black and red spots are lod0 only; the mantle shade against a ring-billed gull's and the head streaking of winter adults are not modelled; immatures not drawn.
